author: N. A. Naylor
title: Central Community Unit School District 301 shares sports updates and scholarship reminders
text:
Central Community Unit School District 301, which serves Kane and DeKalb counties in Illinois, posted updates on its official Twitter account regarding upcoming school events and opportunities for students during April 2026.
On April 7, the district announced a girls soccer home opener: “LUNCHTIME LINEUP: On today’s menu, it’s the girls soccer home opener against Wheaton Warrenville South on Rocket Hill. Remember all home games are played on the Central Campus behind HBT Grade School. TICKETS: https://t.co/Frx7LxHyYP #WeAreCentral https://t.co/NP739aLOfE” .
Later that day, another post highlighted scholarship deadlines: ” This Is the Push April is when many scholarships close. Scholarship Central helps you catch final opportunities before they disappear. https://t.co/t0dxLJFTEU #WeAreCentral https://t.co/2cbVh9GHre” .
On April 8, the district promoted a busy schedule of sports events: “LUNCHTIME LINEUP: On today’s menu, a busy day on Rocket Hill with a little bit of everything for everyone. We have baseball, softball and girls lacrosse all at home! TICKETS: https://t.co/hMyqhu1wau #WeAreCentral https://t.co/x5S8ivogqL” .
Central Community Unit School District 301 encompasses several schools including Central High School and Howard B. Thomas Grade School. The district represents communities in Kane and DeKalb counties ( source ). According to state data, it employs 280 teachers with an average salary of $58,199; most teachers are women (77.7 percent), and there were no teachers with more than ten absences in a school year ( source ). The student body is predominantly White (65.3 percent), with Hispanic (16.5 percent), Asian (12.2 percent), and Black (2.1 percent) populations also represented ( source ). In 2020, per-student spending was $19,244 for a total budget of $84,903,337 ( source ). The chronic truancy rate stood at 1.9 percent—lower than the statewide average of 9.6 percent—with 84 students classified as chronically truant that year ( source ).
